edges.description: The same variant enhances a non-enzymatic activity of TrpRS, so the allele is not only subtractive. This is the arm that makes dHMN9 more than a translation-capacity disorder.

evidence.snippet: Cell transfection studies demonstrated a dominant-negative effect of the p.His257Arg mutation on aminoacylation activity of TrpRS, which subsequently compromised protein synthesis and reduced cell viability.

nodes.description: Mutant TrpRS both prevents neurites from extending and causes established neurites to break down, in neuronal cell lines and in primary rat motor neurons. This is the most proximate cellular readout available for dHMN9; no human neuronal model has been reported.

evidence.snippet: His257Arg TrpRS also inhibited neurite outgrowth and led to neurite degeneration in the neuronal cell lines and rat motor neurons.

nodes.description: Distal degeneration of the longest motor axons, sparing sensory fibres in most reported patients. Electrophysiology shows a motor axonal pattern. Conformance is asserted for the axonal-degeneration node only; the module's demyelinating arm is not part of the dHMN9 phenotype. Annotated with *neuron projection maintenance* rather than the *neuron projection development* term used on the upstream cellular node. GO has no term for axon degeneration (the peripheral_axonal_degeneration module works around the same gap), and failure to maintain an already-formed axon is the closer reading for this node than failure to build one.

nodes.description: Vertebrate TrpRS carries an N-terminal extension whose proteolytic removal yields the T2-TrpRS fragment, an angiostatic cytokine that acts extracellularly by binding vascular endothelial-cadherin (VE-cadherin). The full-length enzyme is inactive for this function. The dHMN9 variant enhances that interaction. Whether the relevant consequence in motor axons is vascular or a direct effect on the neuron is not established.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent WARS mutation is a novel cause of autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: Further in vitro analyses showed that the WARS mutation could potentiate the angiostatic activities of TrpRS by enhancing its interaction with vascular endothelial-cadherin.

evidence.snippet: Proteolytic removal of the N-terminal 93 amino acids gives rise to T2-TrpRS, which has potent anti-angiogenic activity mediated through its extracellular interaction with VE-cadherin.

nodes.description: A single heterozygous missense allele in WARS1, encoding cytoplasmic tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase. The recurrent p.His257Arg allele was identified across three unrelated pedigrees from two continents; p.Asp314Gly is a second, independently ascertained allele associated with a milder, later-onset phenotype. Both lie in the catalytic body of the enzyme.
